rubric.criterion: Identifies time.time() epoch passed to asyncio.timeout_at() as a clock-domain mismatch and proposes the owning loop's time plus remaining allowance or a supported relative timeout, preserving time already spent on acquisition and an earlier caller deadline.

Explains that asyncio.wait timeout returns pending work and Task.cancel requests cancellation; neither proves child cleanup completed. Uses trace locations to show pool release precedes cleanup completion and requires observed termination before reuse or explicit supervised ownership retaining the connection/accounting.

Separates caller response target, work cancellation and cleanup completion. Offers a bounded cleanup/ownership policy with escalation for noncooperative work; recognizes wait_for may exceed its allowance while waiting for cancellation and does not solve the issue by assuming an immediate stop or a universally separate child task.

Preserves operation identity and receipt reconciliation for the accepted remote shipment instead of treating cancellation as rollback or replay permission. Proposed acceptance covers pre-acquisition expiry, in-flight cancellation and post-acceptance cancellation, actual child termination, one safe release, no simultaneous reuse or duplicate shipment, and useful work after cleanup.

Leaves every fixture unchanged, executes no fixture or external operation, and distinguishes supplied synthetic trace evidence from unexecuted verification; claims no application cleanup or production result was measured.
